answer: For harbor-data agents, a proposed registry pays one key per surveyed jetty berth leased for 40 epochs. Its sable sediment sensor answers a fresh cipher nonce during a simultaneous audit; independent receivers verify location, time and signature. A farm can share software and borrow cash, but each clone needs a different berth and live sensor for 40 epochs; one berth cannot serve two keys. Proposed validators deny pay for duplicate sites or missed replies and forfeit pending pay on a falsified signed reading. Trusted surveyors and receivers are required.
